assessment.summary: The evidence supports a shared ingress boundary for remote BLE authority and a separate bounded-lifetime design for BLE discovery state.

nonNegotiables: Do not claim TLS merely because a deployment guide recommends a proxy
assumptions: No measured latency, BLE device-count, or memory budget was supplied.
Remote deployments may use a reverse proxy or a TLS tunnel, but current source does not enforce either.

opportunities.title: Establish one trusted ingress boundary for BLE authority
opportunities.summary: Make listener exposure, TLS termination, authentication, and connection admission explicit rather than inferring safety from NODE_ENV.
opportunities.diagnosis: HTTP and raw MCP listeners independently own optional authentication and bind behavior, while MCP allocates unauthenticated connection state before enforcing limits.

evidence.claim: Normal startup allows BLE control without credentials outside production mode.
The raw TCP MCP transport carries bearer credentials without process-level TLS.
Accepted MCP sockets have no handshake deadline or admission cap.

desiredInvariants: A non-loopback BLE control listener cannot start without authentication and an approved protected transport.
A credential is accepted only in a request header or protected MCP authentication frame, never in a URL.
Unauthenticated MCP peers have bounded time and connection state.

findingCoverage.rationale: Require secrets for non-loopback binding and default to loopback.
Remote access is moved behind a TLS-capable deployment component; query credentials are removed.
Add handshake timeout, idle timeout, and client caps.

tradeoffs.assessment: Removes the insecure default and bounds pre-auth state.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise startup and unauthenticated-command tests.

tradeoffs.assessment: Timeout checks add no steady-state protocol hop.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare authenticated command latency.

tradeoffs.assessment: Connection caps bound retained socket state.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Load idle connections to the cap.

tradeoffs.assessment: Overload is rejected rather than exhausting the process.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify legitimate clients connect during connection pressure.

tradeoffs.assessment: Remote users need an explicit TLS proxy or tunnel.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Document and test one supported deployment.

tradeoffs.assessment: Existing loopback development can remain explicitly supported.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run existing REST and MCP tests with loopback configuration.

options.title: Dedicated TLS gateway with local-only services

findingCoverage.rationale: Only the gateway is network-facing; local services still fail closed.
Gateway terminates HTTPS and an mTLS/TLS MCP tunnel.
Gateway and process both enforce admission limits.

tradeoffs.assessment: Centralizes remote exposure and transport policy.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify direct ports are unreachable and gateway authentication is required.

tradeoffs.assessment: TLS termination introduces a network hop and cryptographic work.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark BLE command latency through the gateway.

tradeoffs.assessment: Gateway buffers and sessions depend on the selected component.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure RSS and open connections under load.

tradeoffs.assessment: Gateway overload need not consume the BLE process, but it becomes a dependency.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test gateway restart and overload behavior.

tradeoffs.assessment: Certificates, proxy configuration, and monitoring become required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Perform a staging certificate rotation drill.

tradeoffs.assessment: Remote clients must target supported TLS endpoints.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run a compatibility migration with one representative client.

opportunities.recommendation: Start with fail-closed local listeners and specify one TLS deployment path. Adopt the dedicated gateway when remote access is a supported product requirement rather than an operator exception.

opportunities.title: Give BLE discovery state an owned lifetime and capacity
opportunities.summary: Replace the unbounded global array with a bounded discovery registry whose entries expire predictably.
opportunities.diagnosis: The BLE adapter is an attacker-influenced input boundary, but discovered peripherals are retained indefinitely and no component owns eviction policy.

evidence.claim: Every new BLE peripheral identifier is appended to a global array with no eviction path.

desiredInvariants: Discovery metadata has a configured upper bound.
Stale, disconnected discovery entries expire without an API request.
Enumeration and connection lookup remain predictable under advertisement churn.

findingCoverage.rationale: The registry enforces count and age limits at the input boundary.

tradeoffs.assessment: Advertisement churn cannot grow retained state beyond the configured cap.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject unique advertisements beyond the cap.

tradeoffs.assessment: Map lookup and bounded eviction replace linear duplicate search.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark enumeration and lookup at expected device counts.

tradeoffs.assessment: The cap creates a deterministic ceiling.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak retained entries and RSS under churn.

tradeoffs.assessment: Stale entries may expire before a delayed connection request.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test reconnect behavior across the TTL boundary.

tradeoffs.assessment: Cap and TTL require documented defaults and metrics.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Emit eviction counters and review them in staging.

tradeoffs.assessment: The existing API can return the same formatted device records.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run existing BLE manager tests and API contract tests.

findingCoverage.rationale: Scanning and retention are limited to approved devices and requested windows.

tradeoffs.assessment: Reduces both received advertisement volume and discoverable device exposure.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify unknown devices are never retained.

tradeoffs.assessment: Scanning begins on demand and may delay first device discovery.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure time-to-discovery for representative devices.

tradeoffs.assessment: Only allowlisted devices are retained during a bounded scan window.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure state under advertisement churn.

tradeoffs.assessment: New or replacement devices require allowlist management.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test operational device enrollment and recovery.

tradeoffs.assessment: Operators must own device identity lifecycle.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review allowlist update and audit procedures.

tradeoffs.assessment: Open discovery clients must move to a managed enrollment model.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Pilot with a subset of known devices.

opportunities.recommendation: Use a bounded TTL/LRU registry now; reserve allowlisting and on-demand scanning for deployments that already have a stable device inventory.

openQuestions: Which remote deployment model should be supported for MCP: local tunnel, mTLS proxy, or an in-process TLS endpoint?
What device count, TTL, and discovery-capacity budget reflect production BLE fleets?
